name: Full installed-app list (QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES)
plain: Android can list every installed app only with a special permission Play restricts; iOS cannot at all.
meaning: The installed-app list reveals religion, health, finance, dating and politics. Android 11 hides it by default; Play approves QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES for a short list of uses.

android.prompt_ui: No prompt; Play review for QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES
android.store_policy: Play: QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES policy, needs core purpose declaration
android.note: Default list is filtered to a small visible set; Play requires a declaration and approval

ios.note: Only canOpenURL probes for up to 50 schemes

limits.headline: Can't list every app on iPhone; on Android only with special store approval
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens in the background when the app asks for the app list
can: Use a full app list on Android if the store approved a security, device management or file manager reason
See a small filtered set of apps on Android 11 and later without approval
Check up to 50 named link types on iPhone
cannot: List all apps on iPhone at all
Get the full list on Android without Play approval
Use the full list for ads or selling data without breaking the store policy
limits.reach_label: Blocked on iPhone, approval only on Android
limits.differs: iPhone has no way at all. Android allows it only with the special all apps permission, which Google approves for few uses.

story.what_it_is: The full list of every app on your phone, which only some Android apps may read.

marketing.name: Package visibility
marketing.pitch: Android 11 hides other apps by default, and Play limits full app list access to approved purposes.

story.for_you: You never see a prompt for it. If an app got the full list, it could tell you take diabetes apps, dating apps or prayer apps, so Android hides it by default.
story.for_makers: A full app list is a rich profile for ads and risk scoring. Antivirus, device management and some banking apps truly need it, so Play approves it only for a short list of cases.

use_cases.example: An antivirus app scans every installed app for malware and warns you.
A work phone management tool checks which apps staff have installed to meet company rules.
A banking app scans for remote access apps that criminals use to take over accounts.
A cheat detection service scans for modding tools next to a competitive mobile game.
A shady ad SDK sells the app list to data brokers as a sign of income and interests.
A device cleaner app finds big unused apps and suggests deletion.

story.android_note: Android 11 and later hides most apps unless the app asks and Play approves the special permission.
story.ios_note: iOS never gives apps a list of other apps at all.

technical_bounds: Visibility is filtered by default on Android 11+

linkedin.how: Play Data safety lists Installed apps under App activity as collected. Reason not stated; Facebook share and login SDKs and share intents are common causes. Unverified.
